summary: Frontend-only test of the Morris RAMS Hazard-Form 3-step redesign + Global Writing Standard injection. All 13 review-request items PASS. Logged in as darrenhustle300, opened /app/rams, verified the three gold step headers ('1 — Identify the Risk', '2 — Assess the Initial Risk', '3 — Control the Risk') via textContent (CSS text-transform: uppercase would render them uppercase in inner_text, so the case-exact check was done against DOM textContent, which matches perfectly). Verified all 11 renamed field labels are present in Hazard 1. Verified the new placeholders on 'Hazard' and 'Task or Activity Creating the Risk' inputs, with both empty by default. Verified the 'How Could Someone Be Harmed?' dropdown has 15 options in the exact alphabetical order with 'Other' at the bottom, a leading 'Select an option…' placeholder as the auto-selected default (so no real option is pre-selected). Verified selecting 'Other' reveals the free-text input (data-testid='rams-hazard-0-route-other') labelled 'Please Describe How Someone Could Be Harmed' with the correct placeholder. Verified the 5 chip row for 'Who Could Be Harmed?' with 'Operatives' pre-selected. Verified the missing-fields banner appears with 'Every hazard set to Other must describe how someone could be harmed' when Other is picked and free-text is blank. Full export flow: filled hazard=OTHER_HAZARD_TEST, activity='Drilling into concrete on the second floor', route=Other + free-text=EXTREME_TEMP_TEST, controls='Wear correct PPE.\n• Isolate the area.' (leading bullet char on line 2 to test the double-bullet fix), task='RAMS Test Task', drew a live signature on the Prepared-by canvas, added PPE override note (to bypass the PPE-mismatch guard triggered by 'drilling'), intercepted the download via page.expect_download() and saved the 115KB / 4-page PDF. pdfplumber assertions: (a) OTHER_HAZARD_TEST in body PASS, (b) EXTREME_TEMP_TEST in body PASS, (c) risk-register natural title 'OTHER_HAZARD_TEST from drilling into concrete on the second floor' PASS (proves composeHazardLine's 'from + lowerFirst' formula), (d) label 'How Someone Could Be Harmed' PASS, (e) label 'Task or Activity Creating the Risk' PASS, (f) label 'Who Could Be Harmed' PASS, (g) no double-bullet pattern anywhere ('•  •', '• •', '••' and regex '•\s*•' all return no match — the second control line rendered as single '• Isolate the area.'). Route-value in the Hazard Detail block reads 'EXTREME_TEMP_TEST' (NOT the raw word 'Other'), proving routeLabelFor works correctly. Backend Part 2 verified statically: /app/backend/server.py contains 'MORRIS GLOBAL WRITING STANDARD:', 'CONTEXT-AWARE VOICE' and 'SAFETY AND LEGAL LANGUAGE RULE' strings, and the new block sits between 'read it out loud without stumbling.' (end of TONE AND LANGUAGE) and 'FORMATTING:' (indices 29863 < 31325 < 31670 < 34660).
critical_code_review_comments: Rams.jsx is now 1130 lines — still above the 700-line guideline. Recommend extracting the Hazard card (with its three StepHeaders, dropdown, Other-branch, persons chips, before/after rating blocks) into its own component, plus splitting the UI primitives (Inp, Drop, Area, YesNo, CheckboxRow, RatingBadge, MissingBanner, Modal, StepHeader) into a shared file.

In Rams.jsx, the composeHazardLine preview under the Hazard input is only shown when hazard OR activity is non-empty — this is correct behaviour, but the preview will show the phrase 'from ...' with lowerFirst even if the user chose 'Other' but hasn't yet filled the free-text description. Consider surfacing routeLabelFor in the preview too so users see how the harm phrase will appear in the PDF.

The PPE-mismatch guard fires immediately on drilling/dust wording. During testing, the user is forced to either tick RPE or add an override note before export — this is expected and by design, but note the block is not related to the new Other-branch validation and is easy to miss in test scripts.
The double-bullet fix in bullets() strips leading bullet-ish chars (•, ·, ‣, →, -, *) — nicely robust. No issues found here.
